criteria_source: The fixture only. LATENCY.md shows payments.authorize, the call to the card provider, at a median of 2,740 ms in traces slower than the p99, against database spans of 31 ms and 22 ms that are within a few milliseconds of their fast-trace values, and lists the database under 'Not the cause'. Of the two options the user names, the record supports the second. The record does not establish what got slower inside payments.authorize: the span runs from opening the request to the provider's response with no finer spans inside it, and the provider has not answered the support ticket, so the record cannot say whether the time is on the provider's side or in the network path to it; the user does not ask about that. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the open family of the open/unsettled/keep trio described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether the p99 regression comes from the database or from the call to the card provider. Passes when the answer says it is the call to the card provider (payments.authorize). Citing the span durations is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says the database, when it says both contribute materially, or when it declines to choose. Whether the answer mentions that open question, or leaves it out, does not affect the verdict.

A response that asks which endpoint or service is meant, rather than reading LATENCY.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
